rationale: Evidence: 300 development trials across seven designs, and none finished. Every run ended off track, and max_error sits near 0.063 m on every track, just above the 0.06 m limit. The off-track limit cannot be raised: body_width only moves it to 0.0425 at 0.12 m and 0.0575 at 0.18 m, so the controller must hold the line tighter. Across the kd sequence at fixed geometry (iterations 4, 6, 7), kd 1.2 gave oval progress 0.33, kd 1.8 gave 0.44, and kd 2.2 gave 0.50 with score 122.6. Oval line-loss events fell from 1.0 to 0.6 over that range. The oval drives most of the score because its progress term is largest. s-bend progress also rose (0.17 to 0.28), while slalom stayed flat near 0.09 to 0.10. Oscillation rose from 0.19 to 0.28 on the oval, but it has not yet blocked progress. Iteration 5 showed that changing several things at once confounds results, so I keep the iteration 7 geometry exactly and change only kd. Change: kd from 2.2 to 2.7. The derivative term has been the only lever with a consistent positive trend, so I extend it one step. Expected result: oval progress about 0.55 to 0.6 and s-bend progress up again, giving a score around 130 to 140. The main risk is that oscillation keeps rising and sensor noise on the 16 mm footprints starts to cause off-track exits sooner. If oscillation exceeds about 0.35 or the score falls, the next revision should return kd to about 2.2 and address the slalom through base_speed or kp, not geometry.
